description:
An `arg_types` column for the shared relation registry — INT-3, blocking, and the only row in this band with a deadline.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored).

A ROLE IS NOT A TYPE. `registry/relations.tsv` and all three domain tables publish exactly these columns: `relation`, `arity`, `arg_roles`, `symmetric`, `tier`, `domain`, `inverse`, `description` — checked against every header, and hardcoded as `RELATION_COLUMNS` in `scripts/check-registry.mjs`, which fails a file whose header differs. `arg_roles` fixes ORDER; nothing fixes TYPE. So for `cine:reads` with `arg_roles` `frame|text`, nothing says whether `text` is a rule-5 LITERAL or a rule-3 IDENTIFIER.

AND KGP §3.2 CANONICALIZES THE TWO DIFFERENTLY. Rule 3 emits an identifier argument as the canonical CURIE — lowercase namespace and kind, NFC, no percent-encoding beyond what the grammar requires. Rule 5 emits a string literal as NFC wrapped in `"` with inner `"` and backslash escaped. Different bytes into `HASH_INPUT`, therefore a DIFFERENT CLAIM ID for one observation, and rule 1 explicitly rests the whole scheme on the registry: 'Arity and the semantic order of arguments are fixed by the registry, so argument order is NOT producer-dependent.' The registry fixes order and leaves type to the producer, which is the gap.

FOUND FROM THE INSIDE, THEN REPRODUCED FROM THE OUTSIDE. koine found it as INT-3 — blocking, with the remedy and the ordering cost in `docs/reference/interop-trial.md` § C3, which already names the fix: 'an `arg_types` column (`id|literal`, positional, parallel to `arg_roles`)'. A producer has since reproduced it independently: its adapter falls back to the `csid` grammar's no-whitespace rule, so `cine:reads(frame-9, "EXIT")` emits an entity CURIE where a peer typing the role as a literal emits a string, and two identical observations DO NOT MERGE. Single-token spans — OCR, sign text, short utterances — are where the divergence concentrates, which is where the vocabulary is densest. An independent reproduction is what raises this from a reading to a measurement.

THE ORDERING IS THE COST. A relation's signature is IMMUTABLE once published — `registry/README.md` states it and gives the reason: changing arity, argument order or symmetry 'would silently change every dependent `claim` id', so a change means a NEW relation name, never an edit in place. The column therefore lands BEFORE the registry has wide production use, or it re-mints every claim that disagrees with it. That is a deadline about adoption, not about effort.

SCOPE NOTE. `scripts/check-registry.mjs` hardcodes the eight relation columns and fails on a header that differs, so the guard moves with the data — that is the check working, not an obstacle. `registry/README.md`'s columns table is the prose statement of the same shape and moves with it too.

userStories.title: The column, on every relation file, with the guard moved with it
userStories.description: `arg_types` positional and parallel to `arg_roles`, per the remedy INT-3 already states.
acceptanceCriteria: Every relation file gains an `arg_types` column — `registry/relations.tsv` and all three domain files (`cinematography.tsv`, `media.tsv`, `social.tsv`) — positional and parallel to `arg_roles`, with one entry per argument position and the vocabulary stated (the remedy in `interop-trial.md` § C3 proposes `id|literal`; a wider vocabulary is allowed only if the fold says why).
Every existing relation is typed — all 29 relation names across the core file and the three domain files, with no position left blank. The count is recorded as observed, not assumed.

`scripts/check-registry.mjs` moves with the data: `RELATION_COLUMNS` includes the new column, so a relation file missing it fails, and the guard still enforces that every file's last column is `description`. The guard failing on the old header is the check working — it is updated, never bypassed.
`registry/README.md`'s columns table gains the row, describing what the column fixes and citing the KGP rules it feeds, alongside the existing rows for `arg_roles` (rule 1) and `symmetric` (rule 2).

GATES: `node scripts/check-registry.mjs` green with the observed row counts recorded, plus `node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` and `bash scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh`.
userStories.notes: 29 relation names typed at every position, no blank (15 core + 5 cine + 5 media + 4 soc; 27 rows id|id, cine:says and cine:reads id|string). Vocabulary widened past INT-3's id|literal to id|string|integer|decimal|boolean|datetime, justified in registry/README.md (rule 5's typed-literal trigger is a judgement, so id|literal leaves R1 vs R3 open, and arg_types is part of an immutable signature so refining it later re-mints claim ids). Guard moved with the data: RELATION_COLUMNS gains arg_types; verified it FAILS on the old header ('registry: 1 error(s) ... a relations file's columns are [relation, arity, arg_roles, arg_types, ...]') and passes after restore. GATES ALL GREEN as observed: check-registry OK, 29 relation names, rows 15/5/5/4; check-doc-integrity OK, 60 markdown files, 1618 relative links, 3 status tables match; check-doc-links --ratchet --base main '0 dead vs 0 on main'; check-schemas OK, 9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures; check-tasklist-categories OK, 12 tasklists; check-roadmap-truth coverage/stale/park all OK.

userStories.title: KGP §3.2 reads the column, so one observation mints one claim id
userStories.description: The column is inert unless the canonicalization rules point at it. Rules 3 and 5 are the two branches that must stop being a producer's choice.
acceptanceCriteria: KGP §3.2 states that an argument's TYPE is fixed by the registry, exactly as rule 1 already states that arity and argument order are — so which of rule 3 (canonical CURIE) and rule 5 (typed literal) applies to a position is read from the registry and is NOT producer-dependent.

The worked case is settled in the text: `cine:reads(frame-9, "EXIT")` canonicalizes ONE way for all producers, and a producer whose fallback heuristic disagrees with the registry is non-conformant rather than differently-opinionated.
A producer with no `arg_types` value to read — an older registry copy, or a relation published before the column — meets a stated rule rather than a silence, and that rule is written down.

The KGP version move is decided under KGP's own rules and recorded with reasoning. KGP is the one RATIFIED spec in this repo, so whether this is a clarification or a normative change is answered explicitly, and if the version moves all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KGP 0.6.0, ratified -> candidate (decided explicitly, not defaulted): MINOR because it is normative surface a reader implements against AND narrows conformance -- a producer conforming to 0.5.2's text could mint a claim id 0.6.0 forbids -- so it is a model-shape change and the README/ECOSYSTEM demotion rule applies; ratified count back to 0 of 6. §3.2 rule 1 now fixes argument TYPE by the registry beside arity/order (id -> rule 3; string|integer|decimal|boolean|datetime -> that branch of rule 5, token-for-token the ARG_TYPES vocabulary US-1 landed), rules 3 and 5 name the positions they are the rule for, rule 5's ^^ form is closed off for a claim argument, and the absent-value rule is written: a position the registry does not type is NOT canonicalizable -- refuse, no default, no fallback, consumer never re-derives or merges. Worked case settled in §3.3 with computed hashes: cine:reads(mediastore:ent:frame-9,"EXIT") -> sha256-1893b75a... conformant; the minted-entity (sha256-a5155f18...) and ^^xsd:string (sha256-f6f292b7...) renderings are non-conformant, not differently-opinionated. Byte-unchanged PROVED, not eyeballed -- sliced both revisions on section headers: SAME for (header excepted) §1, §2, §2.1, §3, §3.1, §3.4, §4, §4.1, §5, §6, §7, §7.1, §7.2, §8; DIFF only §3.2, §3.3, §9, Changelog. All three status mirrors moved (README.md, specs/README.md, ECOSYSTEM.md = 0.6.0 candidate, machine-checked) plus the unguarded 4th (CLAUDE.md) and the count/ranking prose (ROADMAP status line + Phase 0 para + Phase 1 rows, promotability.md, specs/README.md, scenarios/README.md). GATES ALL GREEN as observed: chief verify exit 0 RECORDED for tree d51ddbda (guard-roadmap-truth coverage 50/stale 40/park OK, doc-integrity OK 60 files 1640 links 3 tables match, doc-links '0 dead vs 0 on main', tasklist-categories OK 12, schemas OK 9 schemas 278 positions 80 $refs 3 fixtures, registry OK 29 relation names).

userStories.title: Close INT-3, and say what the deadline was about
userStories.description: The finding is recorded in two places and reproduced in a third. Close it where it lives, with the ordering cost stated so the next vocabulary addition inherits the rule.
acceptanceCriteria: INT-3 is marked closed in `docs/reference/interop-trial.md` with what landed and where, and the independent outside reproduction is recorded as corroboration — an adapter falling back to the `csid` no-whitespace rule, two identical observations failing to merge, the divergence concentrating on single-token spans.

The ordering cost is written down as a standing rule, not as a one-off note: a signature is immutable once published, so a typing column lands before wide production use or it re-mints every claim that disagrees with it. A later reader adding a relation must meet that rule.
The producer that reproduced it is referred to BY ROLE, never by repository or product name — this repo is public and its rows are role-scoped and product-agnostic by design.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: INT-3 CLOSED in docs/reference/interop-trial.md, where it lives: a dated `#### CLOSED — 2026-09-12` subsection under § C3 (what landed in two halves — the arg_types column on all four relation files, 29 relations typed at every position, the guard moved with the data; KGP 0.6.0 §3.2 rule 1 reading it, the ^^ form closed off, the untyped-position refusal), plus a dated banner at the head of the doc, an annotated §6 measurement row, an annotated §8 findings row (INT-3 ✅ CLOSED), §9 item 2 ("One is done — five remain"), and a changelog entry. The C3 heading and its anchor are UNCHANGED (cited from grounding-pack.md, registry/README.md, e2e-worlds-to-fabric.md). The MEASUREMENT IS NOT RE-TAKEN — 1 of 5 at the hash / 0 of 5 as identifiers stands as the reading of 2026-08-18, stated explicitly in three places, and §8's 'nothing here was fixed' sentence is qualified rather than deleted (fixed elsewhere, by the owner, recorded after the fact; ten remain open). Outside reproduction recorded as corroboration with all three properties the AC names: the adapter's csid no-whitespace fallback emitting an entity CURIE where a peer emitted a string, two identical observations not merging with no signal on either side, and the divergence concentrating on single-token spans (OCR/sign text/short utterances) where the vocabulary is densest — and it is what raises INT-3 from a reading to a measurement, since §0 forbids this trial claiming it. BY ROLE ONLY: 'a producer role', 'its adapter', 'a peer'; no repository or product name added anywhere (grepped the diff). ORDERING COST IS NOW A STANDING RULE, not a one-off note: new registry/README.md § 'The ordering rule for a signature-bearing column' — a signature-bearing column lands before wide production use or it re-mints every claim that disagrees with it (adoption cost, not effort), with the two obligations a later reader must meet stated as bullets (a new relation is typed WHEN IT IS MINTED, never after, guard-enforced; a new such column is proposed AT FULL WIDTH, since refining a published token later is an edit in place under another name). The immutability paragraph above it now names argument TYPE as part of the signature (KGP §9 decision 1), the section intro too, and the US-1 one-off note is folded into a pointer. Mirrored in CLAUDE.md's registry bullet; ROADMAP.md's ⬜ row flipped to ✅ DONE 2026-09-12 citing the full stem, and the section's 'Depends on' note updated (the deadline was MET, at 29 relations).
